title: The Pages tab silently drops every pageview whose page_title is empty, though the docs say it shows every URL on the site
statement: pages-tab.mdx states the Pages tab shows detailed analytics for every URL on your site. The tab is fed by GET /api/sites/:siteId/page-titles, whose query filters out rows where page_title IS NULL or page_title = '', and the path is rendered only as the row's subtitle, never as the key. A pageview with no document.title is therefore stored, counted in the overview totals, and present in the pathname dimension, yet entirely invisible on the tab whose subject it is.

handVerified.note: Report section 4, cites correct. Site 15, two pageviews in the same second, one with page_title 'Pricing' on /pricing and one untitled on /docs/getting-started. PROBE GET /page-titles returns exactly 1 row (Pricing). CONTROL GET /metric?parameter=pathname returns 2 rows, and CONTROL GET /overview returns pageviews 2, sessions 2, users 2. The ClickHouse rows confirm both events are stored with the untitled one carrying an empty page_title. Note the board scenario the-pages-tab-lists-every-path-it-has-seen.web.1 PASSES: the seed happens to supply a title for every page, so the corpus never exercised the untitled case. That is a gap in the seed, not a weakness in the finding.

source.howDecided: git log 613cd015..HEAD on all three files returns nothing. At HEAD getPageTitles.ts:72-73 still reads 'AND page_title IS NOT NULL' / "AND page_title <> ''" inside the events WHERE clause, PagesTable.tsx still sources its rows from useGetPageTitlesPaginated (:101, imported :16) and still renders pathname only as the muted subtitle at :155-156, and pages-tab.mdx:8 still reads 'The Pages tab shows detailed analytics for every URL on your site.'

queries: gh api --paginate 'repos/rybbit-io/rybbit/issues?state=all&per_page=100' (not a search; 1044 items, 320 non-PR issues, numbers 1 to 1131 with 87 gaps) then a local regex scan of every issue title plus body

local regex over all 320 issues: page_title|page title|pages tab  ->  4 hits (#658, #617, #559, #368), all unrelated: tracking POST API site_id, custom events not tracked, a ClickHouse JSON column install error, and numeric-string parsing

reevaluation: The finding stands, source untouched, still unreported. This one is a strong filing candidate because the argument needs no timing, no race and no environment detail: two events, one titled and one not, and one of them is missing from a tab documented as showing every URL. It is also the finding with the clearest real-world blast radius, since untitled pageviews are not exotic; they arise wherever document.title has not been set when the tag fires, which is routine in single-page apps that track on route change before the title updates, and on any non-HTML or programmatic pageview. The only thing re-verification changes is a caution for the filer: our own board scenario for this tab passes, because the seed supplies a title for every page, so do not cite the board here. The hand-verification probe on site 15 is the evidence.
notes: Report id F8, hand-verification report section 4. The whole report is four lines of transcript: the page-titles response with one row, the pathname response with two, the overview showing pageviews 2, and the two ClickHouse rows. Put the doc sentence (pages-tab.mdx:8, 'every URL on your site') at the top so the contradiction is the first thing read. State the mechanism in one sentence with the permalink to getPageTitles.ts:72-73 and the observation that pathname is only ever the subtitle, never the key, at PagesTable.tsx:155-156 (so an untitled row has nothing to render as a title, which is presumably why the filter exists). Offer the choice rather than dictating it: either fall back to the pathname when the title is empty, or drop the filter and let the row key on the path, or narrow the doc sentence. This is a good candidate to pair with a small PR if the maintainers respond warmly. rybbit-io/rybbit applies NO labels: all 40 most recent issues carry an empty label array, and both templates declare labels: ''. Do not add a 'Suggested labels' line here; there is no vocabulary to copy and it would only add noise. The bug template is a classic markdown template with bold headers (**Describe the bug**, **To Reproduce**, **Expected behavior**, **Screenshots**, **Desktop**, **Smartphone**, **Additional context**), not a YAML form, and no template-enforcing workflow exists, so there is no auto-close bot to trip.
